---
title: "User guide"
description: "A complete guide to tidymapr: installation, concepts, code, figures, interpretation and reporting."
---

This guide explains how to use tidymapr **and** what its results mean.
Each chapter follows the same plan:

1. **The concept**: the question the method answers, and the theory behind
   it, with its key formula and original references.
2. **Code** you can copy into RStudio, run on real, openly licensed data
   shipped with R packages.
3. **Figures and tables**, made by that code.
4. **How to interpret them**: what the numbers and colours mean, and what
   they do not.
5. **How to report them**: a model paragraph for a methods or results
   section, with the numbers filled in from the analysis.

| Chapter | You will learn | Main functions |
|---|---|---|
| [1. Install and run in RStudio](guide-01-install.html) | Set up R, RStudio and build tools; a first map; your own data; saving figures; troubleshooting | `geo_map()`, `map_*()`, `geo_save()` |
| [2. Cartography concepts](guide-02-cartography.html) | Projections and their distortions; classification methods and GVF; colour schemes; map elements | `geo_automap()`, `geo_automap_explain()`, `geo_classify()`, `coord_projection()` |
| [3. Spatial autocorrelation](guide-03-autocorrelation.html) | Global Moran's I and the correlogram; local Moran's I (LISA); Getis-Ord Gi\* hot spots | `geo_moran()`, `geo_lisa()`, `geo_hotspot()` |
| [4. Interpolation](guide-04-interpolation.html) | Variograms; ordinary kriging and its variance; IDW; cross-validation; kriging with measurement error | `geo_interpolate()`, `geo_diversity_surface()` |
| [5. Species distribution models](guide-05-sdm.html) | Presence-background modelling; Maxent theory and features; response curves; AUC, TSS and Boyce; spatial block cross-validation; ensembles and disagreement | `sdm_maxent()`, `sdm_ensemble()` |
| [6. Remote sensing and terrain](guide-06-remote-sensing-terrain.html) | Spectral indices; Otsu thresholds; spectral diversity; D8 flow; topographic wetness; 3D terrain | `geo_spectral_index()`, `geo_spectral_diversity()`, `geo_flow_accumulation()`, `geo_twi()`, `geo_map3d()` |
| [7. Point clusters and landscapes](guide-07-patterns-landscapes.html) | DBSCAN and its parameters; FRAGSTATS fragmentation metrics | `geo_dbscan()`, `geo_landscape()` |
| [8. Data, GBIF cleaning, web maps and recipes](guide-08-data-webmaps-recipes.html) | GIS, CAD, netCDF and spreadsheet data; cleaning GBIF coordinates; interactive web maps; GeoSpaX recipes | `geo_read()`, `geo_raster_read()`, `geo_clean()`, `geo_webmap()`, `geo_recipe_run()` |
| [9. Distance decay and spatial eigenvectors](guide-09-decay-mem.html) | Similarity against geographic and environmental distance; Moran's eigenvector maps (dbMEM) as predictors | `geo_decay()`, `geo_mem()` |
| [10. Mid-domain effect on maps and in the sea](guide-10-mid-domain.html) | Geometric constraints on richness in two dimensions and along depth | `geo_middomain()` |
| [11. Range shifts under climate change](guide-11-range-shifts.html) | Downscaled CHELSA climate; integrated niche models; dispersal-limited simulation; ensembles of futures | `geo_chelsa_area()`, `sdm_integrated()`, `geo_shift_simulate()`, `geo_shift_ensemble()` |
| [12. Invasions and epidemics](guide-12-invasions-epidemics.html) | Epidemic growth and R; invasion spread rates; dispersal kernels and resistance; spatial epidemics; the tidyvisor | `epi_growth_rate()`, `geo_spread_rate()`, `geo_epidemic_simulate()`, `tidyvisor()` |

**Where to start.** New to R: Chapter 1, then Chapter 2. Need a map for a
paper: Chapter 2. Analysing field samples: Chapters 3 and 4. Working with
species records: Chapter 5. Working with imagery or elevation: Chapter 6. Bringing in your own files or GBIF records, or sharing interactive maps: Chapter 8. Climate change: Chapter 11. Invasive species and disease: Chapter 12.

**Going further.** The [case studies](tutorials.html) apply these
methods to complete research questions, the [Gallery](gallery.html) shows
the code of every map, and the [Reference](../reference/index.html) lists
every function and argument. For diversity estimation itself, see the
companion package [tidydiversity](https://tidydiversity.in4metrix.dev);
for a point-and-click desktop GIS with the same conventions, see
[GeoSpaX](https://geospax.in4metrix.dev).

**How to cite.** Run `citation("tidymapr")` in R.
